director_mandate.scout_assessment: Scout brief was central to this direction. Its synthetic-to-real transfer debt framing, tunnel flag inventory, cross-lane dependency map (runtime -> graph/product, intel -> physics/graph), and external context (WebMCP as shipping Chrome standard, BrowserGym 0.14.3 maturity, VerMem/MemGuard learned verifiers, DSM compilation O(1) economics) were adopted. I challenged its suggestion to add verifier-gated freshness as Graph next gate: adopted as second-order alternative but deferred behind mandatory health-gated transfer which Scout correctly identifies as hard blocker. I accepted its frontier compilation bypass shootout, runtime header-variance fix, and intel orthogonal census pivots as globally most promising. I rejected implicit continuation of alias threshold sweeps and Laplace/DM alpha sweeps that Scout flags as trap.
